articles.title: Big Cat Conservation can be a Powerful Pathway for Climate Change Mitigation: Union Environment Minister at UNFCCC COP31, at Antalya (Türkiye)
articles.full_content:
India’s Tiger Conservation Model demonstrates how Wildlife Protection can strengthen Carbon Sinks, Climate Resilience and Community Livelihoods: Shri Bhupender Yadav
Antalya (Türkiye), 16th November, 2026
Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Bhupender Yadav, today highlighted the critical role of big cat conservation in advancing climate change mitigation and strengthening ecosystem resilience at the High-Level Ministerial Side Event titled ‘BIG CATS: Drivers of Climate Change Mitigation’. The event was jointly organised by the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC), Government of India, and the International Big Cat Alliance (IBCA), at the United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in Antalya, Türkiye. The event brought together Ministers and country representatives from big cat range countries of Nepal, Venezuela, Cambodia, Sri Lanka, besides representatives of international conventions and organisations like the Ramsar Convention and UNCCD.
The gathering saw the dignitaries and conservation experts deliberate on the contribution of big cat conservation and their habitats towards climate change mitigation, ecosystem resilience and sustainable development. The discussions highlighted how conserving the world's seven major big cat species and their habitats can contribute to safeguarding carbon-rich ecosystems, strengthening ecosystem services, enhancing climate resilience and advancing global climate objectives. A presentation was also shown by DG (IBCA), Shri S.P. Yadav on the IBCA and status of big cats in the range countries. The participants appreciated India’s efforts made under the leadership of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi in big cat conservation, especially Cheetah reintroduction.
Highlighted the critical role of big cat conservation in advancing climate change mitigation and strengthening ecosystem resilience at the High-Level Ministerial Side Event titled ‘BIG CATS: Drivers of Climate Change Mitigation’, organised by @moefcc, and the @IBCA_official, at COP31 in Antalya, Türkiye. The event brought together Ministers and country representatives from big cat range countries of Nepal, Venezuela, Cambodia, Sri Lanka, besides representatives of international conventions and organisations like the Ramsar Convention and UNCCD. The participants were appreciative of India’s efforts made under the leadership of PM Shri @narendramodi ji in big cat conservation, especially cheetah reintroduction.
Addressing the event, Shri Yadav highlighted the role of the International Big Cat Alliance (IBCA), envisioned by Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi, in advancing global big cat conservation. Recognising the challenges facing wildlife recovery globally, he said that IBCA provides a platform for sharing India's successful conservation models, facilitating knowledge exchange, strengthening international cooperation and building capacities for the recovery of all seven big cat species across the world.

NITI Aayog holds first National Workshop on “Leadership as a Mission” on the completion of 25 years of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi as Head of Government
articles.full_content:
Dr. P.K. Mishra, Principal Secretary to the Prime Minister, delivers inaugural keynote address at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi
NITI Aayog organised the National Workshop on “Leadership as Mission” at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi today, to draw on the learnings from the twenty-five years of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi as Head of Government. The Prime Minister assumed office as Chief Minister of Gujarat in October 2001 and as Prime Minister of India in May 2014 and has led the Government at the State and the Union levels without a break since then. Throughout this period, he has held public office as a mission of service. His description of himself as the Pradhan Sevak places the citizen at the centre of every office of government, and the principles of Antyodaya, Jan Bhagidari and Sabka Saath, Sabka Vikas, Sabka Vishwas, Sabka Prayas have guided the direction of governance at both levels.
The workshop is the first in a series of five National Workshops. The deliberations and first-hand experiences shared during the series will be developed into case studies and learning material for civil services training institutes, educational institutions and universities. Over the course of the series, the learning from these twenty-five years will also be taken forward through research and teaching material that sets out directions for policy and administration in the years leading up to Viksit Bharat @2047.
More than 900 participants attended the workshop, of whom 250 took part directly in the deliberations. The participants included Secretaries and senior officers of the Union and State Governments, District Collectors of Aspirational Districts, students of educational institutions and universities, and community partners and beneficiaries of national flagship schemes. The proceedings are also streamed on the iGOT Karmayogi platform and at Central and State Administrative Training Institutes, enabling officers from across the country to participate in the programme.
The workshop commenced with the National Song and the National Anthem followed by welcome address by Shri Anurag Jain, Chief Executive Officer, NITI Aayog . He highlighted that the objective of this workshop is to document the learnings from 25 years of leadership of the Hon’ble Prime Minister and translate them into institutional knowledge for the future.
He outlined four key lessons from the leadership journey. First, purpose must take precedence over hierarchical position, shifting the focus from individual leadership to a shared collective mission. Second, service must replace command, with governance centred on reaching the last person in the queue. Third, intrinsic conviction builds resilience, enabling adversity to become an opportunity for societal transformation. And fourth, true empowerment must outlive individual leadership through strong institutions, capable teams and sustainable systems.
Shri Ashok Kumar Lahiri, Vice Chairman, NITI Aayog, delivered the opening remarks. He said,

The Prime Minister assumed office as Chief Minister of Gujarat in October 2001 and as Prime Minister of India in May 2014 and has led the Government at the State and the Union levels without a break since then. Throughout this period, he has held public office as a mission of service.

CAEPHT Organises Two-Day Skill Enhancement Training Programme on Bakery Products and Orange Beverages
articles.full_content:
Ranipool, 17 November 2026:
The College of Agricultural Engineering and Post Harvest Technology (Central Agricultural University, Imphal), Ranipool, Sikkim, successfully organised a Two-Day Skill Enhancement Training Programme on “Preparation of Bakery Products and Orange Beverages” on 16 November 2026 and 17 November 2026, with funding support from ATMA, Namchi, Government of Sikkim. A total of 23 farmers participated in the programme.
Participants received hands-on training in the preparation of millet cookies, buckwheat cookies, muffins, orange Ready-to-Serve (RTS) beverages and orange squash. Practical sessions covered ingredient selection, formulation, processing, baking, beverage preparation, packaging and hygienic handling.
The valedictory programme was held on 17 November 2026 in the presence of Prof. N. S. Chauhan, Dean, CAEPHT. The programme was also attended by Miss Ongmu Sherpa, ATM, ATMA, Namchi; Shri Varun Rai, Agricultural Inspector, Agriculture Department, Government of Sikkim, and other personnel from ATMA, Namchi and the Agriculture Department, Government of Sikkim. The participants shared their written feedback on the training programme. Certificates were distributed, and Prof. N. S. Chauhan encouraged farmers to utilise the skills acquired for entrepreneurship development and income generation.
The programme was coordinated by Dr. Sujata Jena, Department of Processing and Food Engineering, CAEPHT, with the support of faculty members and technical staff. The programme concluded with a vote of thanks, acknowledging the support of ATMA, Namchi, Government of Sikkim, and all those who contributed to its successful conduct.
articles.summary: Ranipool, 17 November 2026: The College of Agricultural Engineering and Post Harvest Technology (Central Agricultural University, Imphal), Ranipool, Sikkim, successfully organised a Two-Day Skill Enhancement Training Programme on “Preparation of Bakery Products and Orange Beverages” on 16 November 2026 and 17 November 2026, with funding support from ATMA, Namchi, Government of Sikkim. A total of 23 farmers participated in the programme. Participants received hands-on training in the preparation of millet cookies, buckwheat cookies, muffins, orange Ready-to-Serve (RTS) beverages and orange squash.

Cabinet Secretary launches Karmayogi Sankalpa at NITI Aayog’s National Workshop on “Leadership as a Mission”
articles.full_content:
Civil servants across the country to record commitments to specific changes in their leadership practice on the iGOT Karmayogi platform
Dr. T.V. Somanathan, Cabinet Secretary, today launched the Karmayogi Sankalpa on the iGOT Karmayogi platform at the valedictory session of the National Workshop on “Leadership as a Mission”, organised by NITI Aayog at Bharat Mandapam, New Delhi. The workshop is the first in a series of five National Workshops being organised by NITI Aayog on the completion of twenty-five years of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi as Head of Government.
Under the Karmayogi Sankalpa, each civil servant records one commitment to a specific change in their own leadership practice. The commitment sets out where the officer will act, the leadership attributes the officer will build, the change that citizens will see, and the action the officer will take. Participants at Bharat Mandapam and officers joining through the iGOT Karmayogi platform recorded their commitments at the time of the launch. The commitments of government officers will be followed up by Karmayogi Bharat. The Sankalpa will be taken forward through Ministries, State Governments and training institutions, with a target of 25,000 commitments to be recorded on the platform by 25 December 2026, which is observed as Good Governance Day.
The day opened with the inaugural keynote address by Dr. P.K. Mishra, Principal Secretary to the Prime Minister, followed by first-hand accounts on the reconstruction of Kutch after the 2001 earthquake, the response to Covid-19, Lakhpati Didi and the opening up of the space economy. In the Case Clinic, each group examined one decision from its assigned episode, considering what public purpose required in the decision, what stood against it, and how the decision was held to its purpose through implementation.
A panel discussion on “Leadership for Viksit Bharat” was moderated by Shri B.V.R. Subrahmanyam, former Chief Executive Officer, NITI Aayog . The panelists were Shri Arvind Kumar Sharma, Cabinet Minister for Urban Development and Energy, Government of Uttar Pradesh, Prof. Vishal Gupta, Indian Institute of Management Ahmedabad, Ms. Debjani Ghosh, former President, NASSCOM and Distinguished Fellow, NITI Aayog, and Ms. Narayani Bhatia, Joint Magistrate, Hardoi, Uttar Pradesh.
The panelists shared their thoughts on Hon’ble Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s leadership principles and their relevance to achieving the vision of Viksit Bharat 2047.
Shri Arvind Kumar Sharma highlighted the paradigm shift in governance during the Prime Minister’s tenure as Chief Minister of Gujarat, emphasizing his ability to create new processes, build institution and human resource capacity and placing local communities at the centre of development.

CAQM Revokes GRAP III in Delhi-NCR, Moves to GRAP II as AQI improves
articles.full_content:
The Sub-Committee on Graded Response Action Plan (GRAP) of the Commission for Air Quality Management in NCR and Adjoining Areas (CAQM) today decided to revoke GRAP STAGE III vide its order dated 17 th November 2026. In view of the improving trend in Delhi's Air Quality Index (AQI), the CAQM Sub-Committee on GRAP met today to review the prevailing air quality scenario in the region. The Sub-Committee also examined the meteorological conditions and air quality forecasts provided by IMD/IITM.
During the review, the Sub-Committee observed that Delhi's AQI has shown an improving trend and was recorded at 204 on 17.11.2026. The IMD/IITM forecast indicates that the AQI is likely to remain in the ‘Poor/Very Poor’ category in the coming days. The Sub-Committee, accordingly, decided to revoke its order dated 06.11.2026, for invoking actions under Stage-III (‘Severe’ Air Quality) of extant Schedule of GRAP, with immediate effect.
The Commission order dated 30.10.2026, restricting the dust generating demolition and outdoor construction activities in the entire NCR barring exempted projects would, however, continue to remain in force (as available on caqm.nic.in ). The order directed State Government and private offices to operate with upto 50% of the staff strength attending physically in the NCT of Delhi and nearby districts as per para 6(i) and 6(ii) of the order respectively for the period 5 th November to 20 th November. Agencies would keep strict vigil and especially intensify measures under Stages I & II of the extant schedule of GRAP to obviate the need for re-imposition of Stage-III of extant GRAP in NCR.
The Sub-Committee also urged citizens to adhere to the following specific steps listed in Citizen Charter of Stage-I along with Stage-II of GRAP and assist in effective implementation of the GRAP measures aimed towards sustaining and improving air quality in the region, as under:
● Check AQI from SAMEER App and stage of GRAP in force from CAQM website.
● Keep engines of your vehicles properly tuned.
● Maintain proper tyre pressure in vehicles.
● Keep PUC certificates of your vehicles up to date.
● Do not idle your vehicle, also turn off the engine at red lights.
● Do not ply end-of-life / visibly polluting diesel or petrol vehicles.
● Prefer public transport or pooling of vehicles for commuting and minimize use of personal vehicles.
● Prefer EVs to control vehicular pollution.
● Ensure segregation and proper disposal of municipal solid waste.
● Do not litter / dispose waste, garbage in open spaces.
● Ensure disposal of waste only in designated collection points provided by municipal authorities, especially in markets and public places.
● Ensure immediate removal of C&D waste and compliances of dust mitigation measures.
● Plant more trees and cover open spaces with grass and shrubs.
● Avoid using DG sets except for essential activities.
● Celebrate festivals in an eco-friendly manner – avoid firecrackers.
● Report air polluting activities through 311

The Sub-Committee also examined the meteorological conditions and air quality forecasts provided by IMD/IITM.

PRESS NOTE ON PERIODIC LABOUR FORCE SURVEY (PLFS) MONTHLY BULLETIN October, 2026
articles.full_content:
Female labour force and workforce participation increased Urban UR declined
Overall LFPR (15+ years) increased to 55.7% in October, 2026, a rise of 0.3 percentage points year-on-year.
Rural LFPR (15+ years) improved to 58.4% in October, 2026, gaining 0.4 percentage points over the past month and 0.6 percentage points over the year.
Overall female LFPR (15+ years) recorded an increase of 0.8 percentage points year-on-year to 35.0% in October, 2026.
Overall WPR (15+ years) improved by 0.5 percentage points year-on-year to 53.0%.
Female WPR (15+ years) recorded at 33.3% an increase of 0.5 percentage points over last month.
Overall UR (15+ years) decreased to 4.9% in October, 2026, 0.3 percentage points lower than a year earlier.
Overall female UR fell by 0.4 percentage points year-on-year to 5.0%, with rural female UR dropping to 3.8%, its lowest level recorded during 2026.
The Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) conducted by NSO, MoSPI, is the primary source of data on activity participation and employment and unemployment conditions of the population. The PLFS survey methodology has been modified from January, 2025 to provide monthly and quarterly estimates of labour force indicators for the country.
Monthly results of PLFS are released in the form of Monthly Bulletins. It presents estimates of key labour market indicators viz. Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR), Worker Population Ratio (WPR) and Unemployment Rate (UR) at the all-India level following the Current Weekly Status [1] (CWS) approach.
The Monthly Bulletins for April, 2025 to September, 2026 have already been released. The present Monthly Bulletin for October, 2026 is the nineteenth in the series.
Key findings for persons of age 15 years and above following CWS:
Rural areas lead the improvement in labour force participation:
The overall Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR) for persons aged 15 years and above improved marginally to 55.7% in October, 2026, compared to 55.5% in September, 2026. In rural areas, LFPR increased from 58.0% to 58.4% over the month, while the urban LFPR stood at 50.5% in October, 2026 against 50.7% in September, 2026.
On a year-on-year basis, the overall LFPR improved by 0.3 percentage points, increasing from 55.4% in October, 2025 to 55.7% in October, 2026. During the same period, rural areas recorded a gain of 0.6 percentage points, with rural LFPR increasing from 57.8% to 58.4%, while urban LFPR remained unchanged at 50.5%.
Overall LFPR reached 55.7% in October, 2026, showing an improvement over both the preceding month and the corresponding month a year earlier.
Overall Female Labour Force Participation increased:
Overall female LFPR improved to 35.0% in October, 2026 from 34.6% in September, 2026, making its highest level since February, 2026. Rural female LFPR rose by 0.6 percentage points over the month and reached 39.5% in October, 2026. However, female LFPR in urban areas remained stable at 25.9%.

Rural LFPR (15+ years) improved to 58.4% in October, 2026, gaining 0.4 percentage points over the past month and 0.6 percentage points over the year. Overall female LFPR (15+ years) recorded an increase of 0.8 percentage points year-on-year to 35.0% in October, 2026.

articles.full_content:
Provisional Wholesale Price Index (Base Year 2022-23) for the month of October 2026
Key highlights of WPI (Base Year 2022-23) for October 2026
• All India Wholesale Price Index (WPI) inflation for October 2026 is 12.29 per cent on year-on-year (YoY) basis, compared to 11.39 per cent in September 2026. The index for All Commodities for October 2026 stands at 113.3, whereas it was 112.5 in September 2026.
• YoY inflation rates for major groups, namely, Primary Articles, Fuel and Power, and Manufactured Products are 9.24 per cent, 32.84 per cent, and 9.54 per cent, respectively in October 2026, compared to 8.67 per cent, 25.85 per cent, and 9.76 per cent, respectively in September 2026. The indices for Primary Articles, Fuel and Power, and Manufactured Products are 120.6, 115.7, and 110.2, respectively, in October 2026, whereas they were 120.3, 110.5, and 110.2, respectively, in September 2026.
• Across groups, ‘Mineral Oils (containing Petroleum Products) ’, ‘Crude Petroleum and Natural Gas’, ‘Electricity’, ‘Food Articles’, ‘Manufacture of Basic Metals’, ‘Manufacture of Chemicals and Chemical Products’, ‘Manufacture of Food Products’, ‘Non-Food Articles’, ‘Manufacture of Textiles’, and ‘Manufacture of Rubber and Plastic Products’ have been drivers of WPI inflation in October 2026.
• WPI Food Index (weight=24.99 per cent): The Food Index consists of ‘Food Articles’ from Primary Articles major group, and ‘Manufacture of Food Products’ from Manufactured Products major group. It observed a YoY inflation of 8.58 per cent in October 2026, compared to 8.66 per cent in September 2026.

MSME-DFO GOA TO ORGANISE ENTREPRENEURSHIP AWARENESS PROGRAMME AND SKILL DEVELOPMENT TRAINING ON ‘TOUR GUIDE’
articles.full_content:
Panaji : 16 November 2026
The MSME-Development & Facilitation Office (MSME-DFO), Goa, Ministry of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME), Government of India, will organise an Entrepreneurship Awareness Programme (EAP) on November 17, 2026, at Chitrakala Hall, Directorate of Art & Culture, Sanskruti Bhavan, Patto, Panaji, Goa.
The programme aims to create awareness about entrepreneurship and encourage aspiring entrepreneurs, particularly local youth, to consider self-employment and entrepreneurship as viable career opportunities.
As part of this initiative, MSME-DFO Goa will also conduct an Entrepreneurship and Skill Development Programme (ESDP) on ‘Tour Guide’, commencing from November 18, 2026. The training is designed to equip participants with essential tour-guiding skills, knowledge of Goa’s rich cultural and tourism heritage, and effective communication techniques. It will help participants explore self-employment and entrepreneurial opportunities in Goa’s growing tourism sector.
The skill development training will be held at Chitrakala Hall, Directorate of Art & Culture, Sanskruti Bhavan, Patto, Panaji, with local support from the Goa State Rural Livelihood Mission (GSRLM), Government of Goa.
Participation in the programme is free of cost. However, seats for the skill development training are limited, and candidates will be shortlisted based on an interview.
Interested candidates, particularly local youth and aspiring entrepreneurs, are encouraged to attend the Entrepreneurship Awareness Programme and take advantage of this opportunity to develop their skills and explore new avenues of self-employment.
For further information and enrolment, interested candidates may contact the MSME-DFO, Margao, Goa.
Source- MSME-DFO, Goa/PIB Panaji | Ambadas Yadav / Priti Malandkar

PM Vishwakarma branding and marketing awareness programmes held in Jorhat and Golaghat
articles.full_content:
The Branch MSME-Development & Facilitation Office (DFO), Diphu, under MSME-DFO Guwahati, Office of the Development Commissioner (MSME), Ministry of MSME, Government of India, organised one-day PM Vishwakarma Awareness Programmes on Branding and Marketing in collaboration with the District Industries & Commerce Centres (DICCs) of Jorhat and Golaghat on 13 and 14 November 2026, respectively.
The programmes aimed to enhance the entrepreneurial and marketing capabilities of PM Vishwakarma beneficiaries through sessions on branding, product design and packaging, pricing strategies, Artificial Intelligence (AI), e-commerce, export promotion, institutional credit, financial literacy and government support schemes.
In Jorhat, Shri Prasenjit Baidya, General Manager, DICC, Jorhat, addressed the participants and emphasised the importance of branding, effective packaging and product innovation in improving the competitiveness of artisan products. In Golaghat, Ms. Manorama Morang, Additional Deputy Commissioner, highlighted the benefits of the PM Vishwakarma Scheme and stressed the importance of skill upgradation, technology adoption and effective marketing in expanding market opportunities for traditional artisans.
Resource persons Shri Simanta Kotoky and Shri Vivek Tiwary, Consultants, State Level Project Management Unit (SLPMU), conducted interactive sessions on the practical application of AI in product development, branding and digital marketing. Shri Dibyendu Nag of the National Institute of Design (NID), Jorhat, deliberated on entrepreneurship development, market positioning, pricing, product packaging, design innovation, e-commerce and sales strategies. Sessions also covered various government schemes, including the Chief Minister's Atmanirbhar Asom Abhijan (CMAAA) and the Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (PMEGP).
Shri Rahul, Assistant Director, Branch MSME-DFO, Diphu, highlighted export opportunities, market linkages, product quality and packaging requirements for accessing domestic and international markets. Financial institutions also sensitised participants on institutional credit, loan facilities, credit history, financial discipline and social security schemes. The Jorhat programme additionally covered cybersecurity awareness and safe digital financial transactions.
Both programmes witnessed active participation from more than 100 PM Vishwakarma beneficiaries and stakeholders each. The Jorhat programme also facilitated on-the-spot Udyam Registration, QR code generation for digital payments and enrolment under social security schemes. Interactive discussions provided artisans with opportunities to clarify their queries and engage with resource persons.
